newsitem.title: UK: Unigate FD says dairy market stable.
newsitem.headline: Unigate FD says dairy market stable.

text.p: British dairy and distribution company Unigate Plc is now seeing a much more stable market for its dairy produce, said finance director John Worby on Monday.

"The market environment is now much more stable. In the butter and milk powder area margins are now stable if at lower levels than last year. The commodity trading side should not see any further deterioration," said Worby in an interview.
The company benefited from a decline in its cost of milk with Milk Marque, which sells 60 percent of the country's milk, from April 1 to 22.1 pence per litre from about 25p in the previous year.

World commodity prices for butter and powder milk, by-products of Unigate's milk production much of which is skimmed or semi-skimmed milk, fell some 13 percent in the year due mainly to the strength of sterling.
In the previous year commodity prices were helped by buying pressure from Russia.
Worby was critical of Milk Marque, the farmer-owned group which supplies more than half the milk in England and Wales.
He said the practice of putting a floor on milk prices was flawed, because the market should be allowed to determine prices, and that the floor has been miscalculated and so set too high.

"The whole system for selling milk is inflexible. The system has imposed on it an artificial floor price. We do not think you need a floor. The market should be allowed to find an appropriate floor. Also we think they have calculated it wrongly," said Worby.
At the same time the price of milk sold to supermarkets fell, said Worby, although this was in part offset by stable prices at 40p a litre on milk sold at the doorstep.
Earlier the company reported a 3.4-percent rise in its pretax, pre-exceptional profits in the year to March 31, 1997 of 129.6 million stg.
Compared with last year, lower commodity prices for butter and milk powder reduced operating profit by about 12 million stg.
The company said the new year had started "reasonably well" in a very competitive market. "We are particularly seeing an improvement in our fresh foods business," said Worby.
"The bacon and ham product side have started the year well and we continue to see growth in sales, benefiting from the launch of new products in Britain and France," he said.

The group's fresh foods profits rose 67.3 percent in the year to 66.4 million stg. Unigate has relaunched its Shape range of yoghurt products and different variants, Tournolive margarine spread and Les Delices St Hubert deserts in France.
